worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.summary: Spin in place and kick three times: each kick sweeps a fan in front of the user and rises in power with each hit (the nth kick adds another multiple). Every kick rolls its own accuracy and a miss ends the string. In sweep form the arc also catches a second target beside the first.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.description: The first kick deals %1$s ice contact damage, for %2$s kicks in a row; each landed kick raises the next by %3$s.
Each kick sweeps a %1$s-degree fan reaching %2$s blocks; each hits for %3$s and the kicks are %4$s s apart.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.widen.on: Wide sweep: every kick sweeps a 170-degree fan in front and catches a second target standing beside it; costs 0.88x power per kick, -4% hit chance, +1 tick between kicks, +2 ticks recovery and +4 ticks cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.widen.off: Focused (native form): every kick sweeps only 70 degrees in front for a heavier single hit; +2% hit chance, -1 tick between kicks and a 4-tick shorter cooldown, at the cost of the target beside it.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.timing: Range %1$s blocks; %2$s s preparation, %3$s s recovery, %4$s PP, %5$s s cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.growth.0: From level %1$s the first kick rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.growth.1: From level %1$s the first kick rises to %2$s and the kicking reach extends to %3$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.use.0: Spin in place and kick three times
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.use.1: Each landed kick makes the next one heavier
worldcombat.skill.tripleaxel.use.2: A wide sweep catches a target beside the first
On (wide): the sweep widens to 170 degrees and catches a second target beside the first, at 0.88x power per kick, -4% hit chance, +1 tick between kicks, +2 ticks recovery and +4 ticks cooldown. Off (focused, the native form): a 70-degree sweep, heavier single-target kicks, +2% hit chance, tighter rhythm and a shorter cooldown, at the cost of the extra target.
Beyond this distance it closes in instead of spinning. This is a close-range move, so a large value often still cannot reach.
